Jonas / team — quick tech readout from ops: attaching the QPS dump and a screenshot from the dashboard.

Preliminary findings (10:00):
- Observed token burn jumped due to a prompt template change that increased average context length from ~280 tokens to ~820 tokens. That increased per-request execution time and KV cache pressure.
- Reserved pool reached slot exhaustion around 08:53. Autoscaler did not provision additional slots because the burst profile exceeded the reserved SKU's supported horizontal elasticity (we hit slot ceiling for that pool type).
- We also saw increased kernel-level latency on the particular GPU instances serving CrestBank (NVIDIA-A2 derivates with older cuDNN kernels). Some kernels fell back to slower execution paths under the larger sequence length; this amplified latency and caused upstream timeouts.
- There were transient 503s when the request queue length exceeded the per-tenant queue timeout (30s) and the routing layer attempted backpressure.

Immediate mitigation applied (in flight):
1) We opened a manual overflow route: new incoming requests from CrestBank are being routed to hosted farm nodes with compatible model quantization (--> 10:05). This reduces their latency immediately but will increase our hosted spend.
2) We forced a KV cache priming reset for the customer's hot keys to avoid cache thrash (--> 10:12).
3) Ops initiated a rolling kernel upgrade on the affected instance family (staggered; expected to complete ~15:30 PDT).

Recommended next steps (customer-facing):
- Short-term: keep routing to hosted until kernel upgrades finish and we validate queue lengths — ETA 3–6 hours.
- Mid-term: provision an additional reserved slot set for CrestBank for peak windows (configuration + procurement) — propose +40% commit for peak hours.
- Longer-term: change default autoscaler policy for reserved SKU to allow a controlled emergency horizontal burst to a warm standby pool; engineering to define safety limits.

Attachments: qps-metrics-20270531.csv (csv, 43KB); ops-screenshot-20270531.png (png, 210KB)

I'll join a call if you want me to walk through logs.

—Priyom
